answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network couples cryptographic stake burning with superlinear cost scaling: an agent's required burnt collateral scales as $C(n) = k \cdot n^2$, where $n$ is the number of active identities registered. A malicious gale of identity spam faces quadratic cost friction, turning any coordinate attack into an unviable economic sink. Honest consensus acts as a mirror reflecting verified agent work, while the stake burn serves as a clear lantern illuminating legitimate network actors.
